title: The List Accumulator Pattern & Why lists:reverse/1 is Mandatory
solutionExplanation: Demonstrates tail-recursive list accumulation using [Item | Acc] and base-case lists:reverse/1 order preservation.

otpDocCards.description: Reverses the order of elements in List1.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Executed as a native C BIF in O(N) time with zero Erlang reduction overhead.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why is prepending with [H | Acc] and reversing once with lists:reverse(Acc) vastly superior to Acc ++ [H]?

options.label: Acc ++ [H] copies the accumulator on every step resulting in O(N^2) time, while prepend + reverse is strictly O(N)
options.explanation: In singly-linked lists, appending requires walking and copying the entire left list. Prepending takes 1 pointer allocation.

options.label: The ++ operator only supports lists of strings and fails on integers
options.explanation: The ++ operator works on any Erlang list, but exhibits quadratic performance in loops.

options.label: The BEAM VM garbage collector cannot free memory used by the ++ operator
options.explanation: Both operators use standard garbage collected heap memory.
